summary: Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based space mission design game built with HTML, CSS, and modular JavaScript. Developed with dedicated engines for spacecraft configuration, physics, orbital mechanics, mission scenarios, data persistence, and real-time rendering, the game lets players build spacecraft, simulate trajectories, and evaluate mission outcomes directly in a web browser.   It addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning aerospace engineering decisions into an interactive simulation. Players configure spacecraft systems, navigate orbital mechanics, and test how design choices impact mission success across structured mission profiles, supported by responsive controls and local save storage for iterative experimentation.   This project is important because real spaceflight requires balancing strict engineering trade-offs where every design and trajectory choice shapes mission viability. By translating orbital physics and mission planning into an accessible, zero-install web experience, Mission Architect lowers the barrier to STEM education and helps learners experience firsthand how engineers plan successful space missions.
details:
Overview and How It Works

Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation game. Players step into the role of a mission designer—configuring spacecraft parameters, selecting mission profiles, and launching simulated flights to test whether their designs can achieve orbital objectives.

The application operates through a modular client-side architecture built around real-time simulation and iterative feedback:

  • Spacecraft and Mission Setup: Dedicated data and configuration modules (data.js, spacecraft.js, and missions.js) define spacecraft attributes, mission parameters, and success criteria.
  • Physics and Orbital Simulation: Custom calculation engines (physics.js and orbital.js) simulate spacecraft motion, forces, and orbital trajectories in real time.
  • Interactive Loop and Rendering: The core game loop (main.js and game.js) coordinates user controls (input.js), updates the visual simulation (renderer.js), displays live telemetry and controls (ui.js), and saves player progress locally (storage.js).

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Because Mission Architect runs directly in standard web browsers using lightweight web technologies, users can launch and play immediately without installing software or needing high-end hardware.
  • Hands-On STEM Education: Instead of learning aerospace principles passively, players actively experience how design trade-offs and orbital mechanics determine mission outcomes.
  • Intended Impact: The project aims to demystify space mission engineering for students, educators, and space enthusiasts—encouraging curiosity in aerospace science and showing how careful planning and engineering trade-offs make real space exploration possible.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

  • Core Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and modular JavaScript (index.html, style.css, and a structured js/ codebase).
  • Software Architecture: Custom browser-based rendering engine (renderer.js), standalone physics and orbital mechanics modules (physics.js, orbital.js), state management (game.js), and client-side data persistence (storage.js).
  • Development Tools: Modern code editor, browser developer tools for real-time debugging and frame-rate profiling, and standard PC development hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Mission Architect bridges the gap between overly simplified arcade space games and complex professional aerospace simulation tools. By pairing an approachable browser interface (ui.js, style.css) with dedicated orbital and physics engines (orbital.js, physics.js), the game turns abstract engineering constraints into an intuitive, trial-and-error creative sandbox. Players do not just pilot a pre-built ship—they architect the mission parameters, observe visual trajectory outcomes, and refine their engineering decisions across successive attempts.

Key Factors Considered

  • Balance Between Realism and Playability: Grounding the simulation in authentic orbital and physical behavior (physics.js, orbital.js) while keeping controls and mission goals accessible to players without an aerospace background.
  • Modular Code Maintainability: Separating rendering, input handling, physics, spacecraft logic, mission data, and storage into distinct JavaScript files so each system can be tuned and expanded independently.
  • Performance and Responsiveness: Avoiding heavy external frameworks in favor of clean native web technologies (index.html, style.css, and vanilla JavaScript) to ensure smooth frame rates and fast load times across everyday devices.
  • Iterative Player Feedback: Incorporating structured mission scenarios (missions.js) alongside local save functionality (storage.js) so players can test, fail safely, adjust their configurations, and learn from each iteration.
